summary: Visual selection depends on the analysis goal: comparisons use bar/column charts, trends use line charts, composition uses treemaps or pie charts (few categories only), relationships use scatter plots.

visual.title: Visual Selection Guide
visual.note: Pie/donut charts become unreadable above 5–7 categories — use a sorted bar chart instead

keyInsight: PL-300 tests visual selection in business scenarios. The exam expects you to choose the most appropriate visual — not just a valid one.
commonTrap: Using a pie chart for more than 5–7 categories. With many categories, slices become unreadable. A sorted bar chart is always the better choice for many-category composition.

miniQuiz.question: A manager wants to see how each of 15 product categories contributes to total revenue. Which visual is most appropriate?
choices: Pie chart
Donut chart
Stacked bar chart
Gauge visual
miniQuiz.explanation: With 15 categories, pie and donut charts become unreadable. A stacked bar chart clearly shows proportional contribution while remaining legible for many categories.

summary: Slicers are on-canvas filter controls visible to users. Filters pane provides report-level, page-level, and visual-level filtering. Report-level filters apply to all pages; page-level to the current page; visual-level to one visual.
keyInsight: Slicers are user-facing and interactive. Filter pane filters can be locked or hidden, useful for developer-controlled restrictions. Sync Slicers connects a slicer across multiple pages.
commonTrap: Confusing page-level and report-level filters. A page-level filter only affects the current page. For cross-page filtering, use report-level filters or Sync Slicers.

miniQuiz.question: A slicer on Page 1 should also filter visuals on Pages 2 and 3. What is the best approach?
choices: Add the same slicer manually to every page
Use Sync Slicers to synchronize the slicer across selected pages
Promote the page-level filter to report level
Use a report-level filter in the Filters pane instead
miniQuiz.explanation: Sync Slicers (View menu) configures which pages a slicer filters and whether it is visible on each page — the built-in solution for cross-page slicer synchronization.

summary: Drillthrough allows users to right-click a data point and navigate to a dedicated detail page pre-filtered to that context. The detail page must have a drillthrough field defined.

visual.title: Drillthrough Navigation Flow
steps: User views summary page — map visual shows regions
User right-clicks a region data point (e.g., East)
Drillthrough option appears in context menu
Detail page opens pre-filtered to East region (final — context carried through)

keyInsight: Drillthrough is for navigating to a detail page with context (e.g., selected product). It differs from drill-down, which expands a visual hierarchy within the same visual.
commonTrap: Confusing drillthrough with drill-down. Drill-down navigates within a visual hierarchy (year → quarter → month). Drillthrough navigates to a different page filtered by a selected value.

miniQuiz.question: Users want to click on a region in a map visual and see a detailed transaction list for that region on a separate page. Which feature should you use?
choices: Drill-down on the map visual hierarchy
Drillthrough to a detail page with Region as the drillthrough field
Bookmarks to navigate between pages
Page navigation buttons
miniQuiz.explanation: Drillthrough sends the selected context (Region) to a dedicated detail page. Users right-click a region on the map and select Drillthrough, arriving at a page pre-filtered to that region.

summary: Bookmarks capture the current state of a report page — filter state, visual visibility, and slicer selections. They enable navigation, view toggling, and guided storytelling.

visual.title: Bookmark Toggle Pattern
steps: Set up two visuals: bar chart and data table (same data)
Hide table → create Bookmark A ('Chart View')
Hide chart → create Bookmark B ('Table View')
Add two buttons: 'Chart' → Bookmark A, 'Table' → Bookmark B
User clicks button — bookmarked state restores instantly (final)

keyInsight: Bookmarks are commonly used to toggle between two views (e.g., chart vs table) using a button, or to create a custom page navigation menu.
commonTrap: Expecting bookmarks to capture all page state by default. You can control per bookmark whether data, display (visibility), or current page state is captured.

miniQuiz.question: A report has a bar chart and a table showing the same data. Users should toggle between them with a button. What is the best implementation?
choices: Create two report pages — one per visual
Use bookmarks with visibility toggling — one shows the chart (table hidden), one shows the table (chart hidden)
Use drillthrough to navigate between the two visuals
Use page navigation buttons to switch pages
miniQuiz.explanation: Bookmarks with visibility toggling allow you to show/hide visuals. Assign one bookmark to show the chart and another to show the table. Buttons are linked to each bookmark to trigger the toggle.

summary: Conditional formatting applies dynamic visual formatting — changing background color, font color, data bars, or icons based on data values, rules, or measures.

visual.title: Conditional Formatting Color Rules
visual.note: Use a DAX measure for per-row dynamic thresholds — fixed rules cannot vary by context

keyInsight: Conditional formatting can use field values, threshold rules, or DAX measures. Using a measure allows fully dynamic logic that responds to context — not possible with simple rules.
commonTrap: Using a fixed threshold rule when the threshold should vary by row or context. A fixed rule cannot compare against a per-row target — a measure is required.

miniQuiz.question: A table visual should highlight cells red when sales fall below each region's individual target. The target differs per region. How should conditional formatting be configured?
choices: Use a fixed threshold rule: if sales < 1000, color red
Create a measure comparing sales to the region target and apply measure-based conditional formatting
Use icon sets with three categories
Enable data bars on the sales column
miniQuiz.explanation: A measure can compare each region's sales against its specific target dynamically and return 'Red' or 'White'. This is applied in conditional formatting to produce per-region, context-aware color highlighting.

summary: Paginated reports are designed for pixel-perfect, print-ready output. They display all data across multiple pages — unlike standard Power BI reports that limit visual data points. Built using Power BI Report Builder.
keyInsight: Paginated reports are the correct choice for: invoices, formal statements, regulated disclosures, or any scenario where every data row must appear. Standard reports are better for interactive exploration.
commonTrap: Using standard Power BI reports for high-volume printing. Standard visuals truncate data. Paginated reports are required when all data must appear across pages.

miniQuiz.question: A finance team needs monthly invoices for 5,000 customers, each requiring a separate printable page with precise formatting. Which solution is appropriate?
choices: A standard Power BI report with page navigation
A paginated report built in Power BI Report Builder
A Power BI dashboard exported to PDF
A dataflow with scheduled email delivery
miniQuiz.explanation: Paginated reports are designed for pixel-perfect, print-ready output with one record per page. They handle thousands of pages efficiently and support parameters for filtering by customer.

summary: Power BI AI visuals include: Key Influencers (identifies statistical drivers of a metric), Decomposition Tree (manually breaks down a measure across dimensions), and Q&A (natural language queries).

visual.title: AI Visual Selection Guide
rows: Finds statistical drivers of a metric
Why is churn high? What drives revenue?
Explore a measure by any dimension interactively
Let users ask questions in plain English
Add dynamic written insights to a report
visual.note: Key Influencers = automatic analysis; Decomposition Tree = manual exploration

keyInsight: Know when to use each: Key Influencers = 'why is X high/low?'. Decomposition Tree = 'break down X by multiple dimensions interactively'. Q&A = 'let users ask natural language questions'.
commonTrap: Using Decomposition Tree when Key Influencers is the right answer. Decomposition Tree explores data manually; Key Influencers automatically identifies statistically significant drivers.

miniQuiz.question: A business analyst wants to understand which factors most influence customer churn. Which AI visual should be used?
choices: Decomposition Tree
Q&A visual
Key Influencers
Smart Narrative
miniQuiz.explanation: Key Influencers analyzes a metric (churn) and automatically identifies which factors (age, plan type, region, etc.) have the most statistical influence on the outcome — the correct fit here.

summary: Power BI Desktop allows you to create a dedicated phone layout for each report page. Visuals can be rearranged and resized independently of the desktop layout for optimal mobile viewing.

visual.title: Mobile Layout Configuration Steps
steps: Design report in normal desktop canvas view
Go to View tab → click Mobile Layout
Phone canvas appears — drag existing visuals onto it
Resize and reorder visuals for portrait phone screen
Publish report — mobile users see the phone layout automatically (final)

keyInsight: Mobile layouts are configured in View > Mobile Layout. Each page has its own mobile layout. Only visuals placed on the mobile canvas appear on mobile devices.
commonTrap: Assuming the desktop layout automatically adapts to mobile. It does not — without a configured mobile layout, Power BI shows a simplified, auto-arranged view that may not look professional.

miniQuiz.question: A sales report needs a fully custom layout optimized for smartphones. What should you configure?
choices: Enable responsive design in report settings
Create a separate PBIX file specifically for mobile
Configure the Mobile Layout for each report page in Power BI Desktop
Set report page dimensions to 375 × 812 pixels
miniQuiz.explanation: Mobile Layout (View tab in Desktop) allows you to design a phone-optimized arrangement of existing visuals for each report page — the built-in, correct solution for mobile-optimized reports.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
summary: Custom tooltips replace the default hover popup with a full report page you design. The tooltip page shows additional context when users hover over a data point — charts, KPIs, tables — without leaving the main visual.

visual.title: Default vs Custom Tooltip
visual.note: Set page type to 'Tooltip' in Page Information. Then assign the tooltip page to a visual via Format > Tooltips > Report page.

keyInsight: Custom tooltip pages are full report pages with Page type set to 'Tooltip'. You can include any visual on them — a trend line, a mini KPI card, a comparison chart — all shown on hover.
commonTrap: Forgetting to set the page type to 'Tooltip' in Page Information. Without this, the page cannot be assigned as a tooltip to any visual and does not display on hover.

miniQuiz.question: A product manager wants hovering over a bar chart category to show a mini trend line for that category's sales over the last 12 months. Which feature supports this?
choices: Add a tooltip field to the visual using the Fields pane
Create a report page with Page type set to Tooltip, add the trend line visual, then assign it as the report page tooltip on the bar chart
Enable the built-in analytics pane trend line and configure it to appear on hover
Use a bookmark that activates when a user hovers over a bar
miniQuiz.explanation: Custom tooltip pages allow rich visuals (including a full line chart) to appear on hover. Set the page type to Tooltip, design the content, then assign the page under Format > Tooltips > Report page on the target visual.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
summary: By default, clicking a data point in one visual cross-filters or cross-highlights all other visuals on the page. Edit Interactions lets you change this behavior per visual pair — switching to cross-highlight, filter, or none.

visual.title: Interaction Types Between Visuals
rows: Removes non-matching rows from target visual
When selection should hide unrelated data
When you want context preserved visually
visual.note: Enable Edit Interactions from the Format tab. The icons appear above each target visual — click to set the behavior.

keyInsight: Cross-filter removes non-matching data from the target visual completely. Cross-highlight keeps all data visible but dims non-selected portions. 'None' makes a visual completely ignore selections on the page.
commonTrap: Confusing cross-filter and cross-highlight. Cross-filtering changes totals (data is removed), while cross-highlighting keeps totals the same (data is visually dimmed but still present in the aggregation).

miniQuiz.question: A report has a bar chart and a KPI card showing total company revenue. Selecting a region on the bar chart should NOT change the KPI total — it must always show the company-wide figure. What interaction type should be set?
choices: Cross-filter — so only the selected region's revenue shows in the KPI
Cross-highlight — so the region portion is highlighted in the KPI
None — the KPI card ignores all other visual selections
Drill-down — so the KPI expands when a region is selected
miniQuiz.explanation: Setting the interaction from the bar chart to the KPI card as 'None' means the KPI ignores all selections on the page and always shows the full company total — exactly the requirement.

summary: Sync Slicers (View > Sync Slicers pane) configures a slicer to filter multiple pages simultaneously. A slicer can be synchronized to any combination of pages — and configured to be visible on some pages but hidden on others while still filtering them.

visual.title: Sync Slicers Configuration Options
rows: Slicer changes propagate to all synced pages
Can be synced but hidden — filters without visual
Disabled by default — requires explicit opt-in
Syncs multiple slicer instances as one
Useful when same field appears as slicer on each page
visual.note: A slicer can SYNC (filter) a page without being VISIBLE on it — the slicer is hidden but its selection still applies.

keyInsight: Sync and Visible are independent settings. A slicer can be synced (actively filtering) to a page while being invisible on it — allowing a global filter to be set from one page without cluttering others.
commonTrap: Assuming synced means visible. If you add a slicer to Page 1 and sync it to Page 2, users won't see the slicer on Page 2 unless you also enable Visible for Page 2.

miniQuiz.question: A date slicer on the Overview page should filter both the Overview and Detail pages, but should only be visible on the Overview page. How should Sync Slicers be configured?
choices: Enable Sync and Visible for Overview; enable Sync only (not Visible) for Detail
Enable Sync and Visible for both Overview and Detail pages
Enable Visible for both pages; Sync is automatic once Visible is enabled
Enable Sync for Overview only — synced slicers automatically filter all other pages
miniQuiz.explanation: Sync controls which pages the slicer filters; Visible controls which pages display the slicer. Enable both for Overview (filter + show); enable Sync only for Detail (filter without displaying the slicer).

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
summary: The Selection pane (View > Selection) shows all visuals on the page as a stacked list. You can reorder the visual Z-order (which appears on top), toggle visibility (eye icon), and group visuals together for collective formatting or animation.

visual.title: Selection Pane Capabilities
rows: Place a shape behind a chart; show image under KPIs
Click eye icon next to visual name
Hide/show visuals — used with bookmarks for toggles
Animate or format multiple visuals as one unit
Makes bookmark targeting and management clearer
visual.note: Renaming visuals in the Selection pane makes bookmark creation much easier — 'Sales Chart' is clearer than 'BarChart1' when setting visibility per bookmark.

keyInsight: The Selection pane is essential for bookmark-based view toggling: hide the visual → capture bookmark → show it → capture another bookmark. Naming visuals here makes this workflow manageable.
commonTrap: Toggling visibility directly on the canvas during design and expecting bookmarks to remember it. Bookmarks only capture the state at the moment of creation — always use the Selection pane eye icon in the correct state before capturing each bookmark.

miniQuiz.question: A report developer needs to layer a text box label on top of a background image and behind a chart. Which tool controls the visual stacking order?
choices: Format pane → Position settings for each visual
View > Selection pane — drag visuals up or down the Z-order list
Right-click canvas → Arrange → Bring to Front / Send to Back
Both B and C are correct and achieve the same result
miniQuiz.explanation: Both the Selection pane (drag Z-order) and right-click Arrange (Bring to Front / Send to Back / Forward / Backward) control visual stacking order. Both methods achieve the same result and are equally valid.

summary: Auto page refresh (available in DirectQuery/Dual mode) automatically re-queries the data source on a set interval. Two modes: Fixed interval (queries on a schedule) and Change detection (queries a special measure to check if data changed before refreshing visuals).

visual.title: Auto Page Refresh Modes
rows: Queries a detection measure first; only refreshes visuals if data changed
visual.note: Auto page refresh requires DirectQuery or Dual storage mode — Import mode stores a snapshot and cannot auto-refresh from source.

keyInsight: Change detection mode reduces query load by only triggering a full visual refresh when the change detection measure returns a new value — ideal for near-real-time dashboards where data changes infrequently.
commonTrap: Expecting auto page refresh to work with Import mode. It does not — Import data is a snapshot loaded at refresh time. Auto page refresh requires DirectQuery or Dual mode to query the source on each interval.

miniQuiz.question: A manufacturing floor dashboard needs to update every 30 seconds but only when machine status data actually changes, to minimise database load. Which auto page refresh mode is most appropriate?
choices: Fixed interval set to 30 seconds
Change detection mode with a DAX measure that returns the latest timestamp — visuals only refresh when the timestamp changes
Import mode with a scheduled dataset refresh every 30 seconds
Incremental refresh configured at the 30-second granularity
miniQuiz.explanation: Change detection checks a specified measure (such as MAX(MachineStatus[UpdateTimestamp])) every interval. Visuals only re-query when the value changes — reducing unnecessary database queries when data is unchanged.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
summary: Power BI supports on-canvas navigation buttons that link to pages, bookmarks, URLs, or drillthrough destinations. Button actions include: Back, Bookmark, Page navigation, Drillthrough, Q&A, and Web URL.

visual.title: Button Action Types
rows: Link to source system or documentation
visual.note: The 'Back' button on drillthrough destination pages automatically returns users to where they came from — no manual page link needed.

keyInsight: The 'Back' button action uses navigation history — it always returns to the previous page regardless of where the user came from. This is the standard pattern for drillthrough return navigation.
commonTrap: Adding a manual 'Back to Summary' page navigation button that always goes to a fixed page. If users arrive from different pages, the Back action is more flexible — it returns them to whichever page they navigated from.

miniQuiz.question: A drillthrough detail page should return users to whichever page they came from when they click a 'Return' button. Which button action type should be used?
choices: Page navigation action pointing to Page 1
Bookmark action pointing to the original page bookmark
Back button action — it uses navigation history to return to the previous page
Drillthrough action in reverse — from detail back to summary
miniQuiz.explanation: The Back button action uses Power BI's navigation history — it always returns to the page the user navigated from, regardless of the source page. This makes it more flexible than a fixed Page navigation link.

summary: Grouping combines specific values into custom named categories. Binning automatically creates evenly-spaced numerical or date ranges. Clustering uses machine learning to detect natural groupings in scatter plot data.

visual.title: Three Analytical Grouping Techniques
rows: Manually select values → assign to a named group
visual.note: Grouping and binning create a new field in the field list — reusable across visuals. Clustering assigns a cluster label to each data point in the scatter visual.

keyInsight: Binning is for continuous numeric/date data (auto-creates ranges). Grouping is for discrete categories (manually combine specific values). Both create reusable fields in the data pane — they are not visual-specific.
commonTrap: Using binning when grouping is needed (or vice versa). Binning creates even-sized numeric ranges automatically. Grouping is manual — you select which specific values belong together. Use grouping for custom category combinations.

miniQuiz.question: A report needs to group customers by age into ranges: Under 25, 25–44, 45–64, 65+. The Age column is numeric. Which feature should be used?
choices: Grouping — manually select age values and assign them to named groups
Binning — automatically creates equal-width age ranges
Clustering — detects natural age groupings from scatter plot data
A DAX calculated column with IF()/SWITCH() logic
miniQuiz.explanation: The required age bands (Under 25, 25–44, 45–64, 65+) are not equal-width — standard binning creates equal intervals (e.g., 0–21, 22–43). A DAX calculated column with SWITCH() defines the exact custom boundaries. Grouping works for discrete values, not continuous ranges.

concept: Reference Lines, Error Bars, and Forecasting
summary: The Analytics pane (accessed in visual Focus mode) adds statistical overlays: constant reference lines, min/max/average/median lines, percentile lines, error bars, trend lines, and forecast lines with confidence bands.

visual.title: Analytics Pane Features
rows: Running mean or median of plotted data
Uncertainty or variance range per data point
visual.note: Forecasting is only available on line charts with a continuous time axis. It uses exponential smoothing — not available for bar or column charts.

keyInsight: Forecast lines (with confidence bands) are only available on line charts with a continuous date/time X axis. You must set the seasonality explicitly or let Power BI detect it — but the model is exponential smoothing, not a full ML model.
commonTrap: Adding a forecast to a bar chart or a line chart with a categorical (non-date) X axis. Forecasting requires a continuous time axis — without it, the Forecast option does not appear in the Analytics pane.

miniQuiz.question: A line chart showing monthly revenue over the last 24 months needs a projected trend for the next 6 months with a 95% confidence band. Where should this be configured?
choices: Format pane → Data labels → enable Forecast
Analytics pane → Forecast → set forecast length and confidence interval
Insert a calculated column with future date rows and NULL revenue values
Use the Q&A visual and ask 'show forecast for next 6 months'
miniQuiz.explanation: The Analytics pane for a line chart includes a Forecast section — set the number of periods to forecast and the confidence interval percentage (e.g., 95%). Power BI uses exponential smoothing to project the trend with upper and lower confidence bands.

summary: PL-300 tests accessibility features: alt text for visuals (for screen readers), tab order (keyboard navigation sequence), high-contrast themes, and ensuring color is not the only means of conveying information.

visual.title: Accessibility Checklist for PL-300
rows: Format pane → General → Alt text (static or DAX measure)
Keyboard users navigate visuals in logical sequence
Report theme or OS setting detection
Add data labels, markers, or patterns in addition to color
Colorblind users can distinguish data series
visual.note: Alt text can be a static string or a dynamic DAX measure — use a measure when the alt text should reflect the current data (e.g., 'Total revenue is $4.2M this quarter').

keyInsight: Alt text for visuals is configured in Format pane > General > Alt text, not in report settings. A DAX measure can generate dynamic alt text that changes with filter context — useful for KPI visuals.
commonTrap: Setting a static alt text string for a KPI visual. If the KPI value changes with filters, a static alt text ('Revenue is $4.2M') becomes inaccurate. Use a DAX measure for dynamic alt text that always reflects the current filtered value.

miniQuiz.question: A report must be accessible to users who rely on screen readers. The KPI card showing current quarter revenue should announce the actual value to screen readers as it changes with slicer selections. How should alt text be configured?
choices: Add a static alt text string: 'This card shows quarterly revenue' in Format > General > Alt text
Enable the 'Screen reader' toggle in Report Settings
Write a DAX measure returning the current revenue as a formatted string, and reference it as the alt text in Format > General > Alt text
Use a text box visual next to the KPI card to display the value as screen-reader-readable text
miniQuiz.explanation: A DAX measure can return a dynamic text string (e.g., 'Current quarter revenue: ' & FORMAT([Revenue], '$#,##0')) that updates with filter context. Referencing this measure as alt text means screen readers always announce the current value.

subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
summary: Personalize Visuals allows report consumers to modify visuals in published reports — swapping fields, changing visual type, adjusting axes — without editing the underlying report. Changes are saved per-user in the Power BI Service.

visual.title: Personalize Visuals — What Users Can Change
rows: No access to model or relationships
Share their personalized view as the default
visual.note: Personalize Visuals is enabled per report in File > Report Settings. When users publish or share the report, recipients see the original author's version — not the personalized view.

keyInsight: Personalization is user-specific and saved in the Power BI Service. When a user shares the report URL, recipients see the original design — not the personalized version. Personalization cannot be embedded in a published snapshot.
commonTrap: Expecting personalized views to persist when re-publishing the report. Re-publishing resets all user personalizations back to the report default. Users need to re-apply their preferences after each republish.

miniQuiz.question: A report author enables Personalize Visuals. A user personalizes a bar chart into a line chart and shares the report URL with a colleague. What does the colleague see?
choices: The line chart — personalized views are shared via the URL
The original bar chart — personalizations are user-specific and not shared through the URL
An error — only the report author can view customized visuals
A prompt asking the colleague which version to view
miniQuiz.explanation: Personalized views are stored per-user in the Power BI Service. Sharing the report URL gives the recipient the original published version — personalizations are not embedded in or transmitted through the URL.

summary: The Decomposition Tree is an AI visual that allows users to break down a measure across multiple dimensions interactively. Users add dimensions one at a time — either manually choosing a dimension or using AI splits (High value / Low value) to find the largest contributor.

visual.title: Decomposition Tree vs Key Influencers
rows: Breaking down a KPI by multiple dimensions
Finding what statistically impacts a metric
'What is driving high returns by category?'
visual.note: Lock a level in the Decomposition Tree to prevent users from changing it — useful when the first breakdown dimension is always required.

keyInsight: The Decomposition Tree's 'AI split' feature suggests which dimension value contributes most to the measure at each level — it bridges manual exploration with AI assistance. But unlike Key Influencers, the user still controls the navigation path.
commonTrap: Using a Decomposition Tree to find the root cause of a metric automatically. Key Influencers does this — the Decomposition Tree requires users to select each dimension level manually. For automated root-cause, Key Influencers is the correct answer.

miniQuiz.question: A logistics manager wants to explore where delivery delays are concentrated — starting by region, then by carrier, then by product category — choosing the dimensions in that order. Which visual is most appropriate?
choices: Key Influencers — it automatically identifies the top drivers of delivery delays
Decomposition Tree — allows the manager to break down delays by region, then carrier, then product in a specific order
Scatter chart — shows the correlation between delay time and each dimension
Matrix visual — shows delays in a grid of region × carrier
miniQuiz.explanation: The Decomposition Tree allows the user to manually navigate through dimension levels in a chosen order — region first, then carrier, then product. Key Influencers would automatically find drivers but not allow user-directed exploration in a specific sequence.

summary: Report themes apply consistent visual styling — colors, fonts, visual defaults, and background settings — across all visuals on all report pages in a single action. Themes are JSON files that can be imported or selected from the built-in gallery.

visual.title: What Report Themes Control
rows: Light grey, white, or custom hex
All pages (can be overridden per page)
Font family, size, color for labels
visual.note: A theme changes formatting for newly added visuals and globally resets existing visual defaults. Per-visual manual formatting overrides the theme for that specific visual.

keyInsight: Report themes apply globally but can be overridden per visual. If you manually format a visual's color and then change the theme, the manually formatted visual retains its color — manual formatting takes precedence over the theme.
commonTrap: Expecting a theme change to override manual per-visual formatting. Manual formatting (set in the Format pane for a specific visual) persists even when the theme changes. Only visuals using default theme settings update when the theme is swapped.

miniQuiz.question: A BI team creates a corporate report theme with brand colors and imports it. One bar chart was manually formatted with a bright red color before the theme was applied. After importing the theme, the bar chart remains red. Why?
choices: The theme import failed — themes cannot override existing visuals
Manual per-visual formatting takes precedence over the theme — the bar chart keeps its manually set color
The theme only applies to new pages added after the import
Bar charts are excluded from theme color settings by default
miniQuiz.explanation: Per-visual manual formatting overrides the theme for that specific element. The theme sets defaults, but any explicit formatting applied to an individual visual persists. To reset to the theme, use 'Reset to default' for the formatted visual property.

summary: Visuals can be sorted by any field in their field well. Sorting options: ascending/descending, by a different field (sort by column), or alphabetically. The 'Sort by column' feature in the model allows a dimension's display order to be controlled by a numeric sort key.

visual.title: Sorting Options and Their Use Cases
rows: Rank highest/lowest values in a bar chart
Sort product names alphabetically but chart by revenue
Create sort index column in Power Query
Fiscal quarters: Q3, Q4, Q1, Q2
visual.note: Month names sort alphabetically by default (April, August...). Fix: create a MonthNumber column, then set Sort by Column on MonthName to MonthNumber in the model.

keyInsight: Month names and day names sort alphabetically by default in Power BI. The fix is always 'Sort by Column' in the Modeling tab — point the text field at a numeric key column. This is a very common PL-300 exam scenario.
commonTrap: Trying to fix month name ordering inside the visual sort menu. The visual sort can only choose which field to sort by — it cannot override alphabetical sorting of a text field. The model-level 'Sort by Column' setting is required to control sort order for text fields.

miniQuiz.question: A line chart shows monthly revenue with months along the X-axis. The months appear in alphabetical order (April, August, December...) instead of January–December. What is the correct fix?
choices: In the visual's sort menu, select Sort descending
Rename months to 01-January, 02-February, etc. so they sort correctly
In the Modeling tab, set Sort by Column on MonthName to a MonthNumber (1–12) column
Use a slicer to reorder the months before they appear on the axis
miniQuiz.explanation: Sort by Column (Modeling tab) tells Power BI to use a numeric MonthNumber column (1 = January, 12 = December) to determine the sort order of the MonthName text field. This is the correct, model-level solution that works across all visuals.

summary: Visual calculations are DAX expressions written directly on a visual — not stored in the data model. They operate on the visual matrix (the data as displayed) rather than the underlying table, enabling running totals, ranks, and moving averages without complex model-level DAX.

visual.title: Visual Calculations vs Model Measures
rows: On the visual itself (not the model)
Uses visual matrix rows/columns as context
Visual-only — not available in other visuals
Available to any visual in the report
Running totals, ranks within a specific visual
visual.note: Visual calculations use ROWS/COLUMNS as context axes instead of filter context — PREVIOUS(SalesAmount) returns the previous row in the visual matrix, not the previous date in the model.

keyInsight: Visual calculations are scoped to the visual matrix — they are ideal for visual-specific running totals, percent-of-parent, and rank within the displayed data. They are NOT available in other visuals or reports — they live only on the visual where they are defined.
commonTrap: Using a visual calculation when the same logic is needed across multiple visuals. Visual calculations are not reusable — they exist only on the visual where they are written. For shared logic, write a model-level measure.

miniQuiz.question: A matrix visual showing quarterly sales by region needs a running total column that accumulates sales left to right across quarters within each region row. Which approach requires the LEAST effort and no model changes?
choices: Write a CALCULATE measure with DATESYTD to accumulate by date
Add a visual calculation using RUNNINGSUM on the SalesAmount value
Create a calculated column in the data model using EARLIER
Use TOTALYTD in a new measure added to the data model
miniQuiz.explanation: RUNNINGSUM is a visual calculation function that accumulates values across the visual matrix axis without any model changes. It operates on the visual's displayed rows/columns — the simplest solution for a within-visual running total.

summary: Subscriptions send scheduled email snapshots of a report page or dashboard at defined intervals. Data alerts notify a user when a dashboard tile's value crosses a specified threshold — alerts only work on KPI-style tiles (numeric) in dashboards.

visual.title: Subscriptions vs Data Alerts
rows: Email snapshot of report page / dashboard
visual.note: Data alerts are evaluated at each scheduled refresh — if the dataset only refreshes daily, alerts can only fire once per day maximum, even if data changes intra-day.

keyInsight: Data alerts only work on dashboard tiles (pinned from reports or built on the dashboard). They cannot be set on report page visuals directly. Alerts fire when a threshold is crossed at the time of dataset refresh.
commonTrap: Expecting a data alert to fire in real time when data changes. Alerts are evaluated at each dataset refresh — if a dataset refreshes once per day, the alert fires at most once per day, even if the underlying source data changed hours earlier.

miniQuiz.question: A sales manager wants an email notification when total revenue for the month drops below $500K. The Power BI dataset refreshes once daily. Which feature provides this, and what is the maximum alert frequency?
choices: A subscription set to daily delivery, which will notify when revenue drops below threshold
A data alert set on the revenue dashboard tile — fires at most once per day (each scheduled refresh)
A report-level filter that triggers email when the threshold is breached in real time
An Azure Logic App connected to the Power BI REST API for real-time threshold monitoring
miniQuiz.explanation: Data alerts must be configured on a dashboard tile (pin the revenue visual to a dashboard first). The alert is evaluated at each dataset refresh — once per day in this case. Subscriptions send scheduled snapshots but do not check thresholds.
